exit_codes.name: ok
exit_codes.meaning: the command did what it was asked; no gate failed and nothing broke.

exit_codes.name: configured-gate-failed
exit_codes.meaning: a quality gate YOU configured failed — for example --min-quality was not met.
exit_codes.remedy: fix the regression, or change the gate. This is not a tool failure, and retrying will not change it.

exit_codes.name: operational-error
exit_codes.meaning: the tool broke, or a platform-facing command could not reach the platform.
exit_codes.remedy: retry, check connectivity, or file a bug. Your workflow is not necessarily worse than it was.

exit_codes.name: invalid-config
exit_codes.meaning: the invocation is malformed: a missing required input, an unreadable config file, a flag out of range.
exit_codes.remedy: fix the invocation. The message names the input that was missing rather than reporting a generic flag error.

metrics.name: latency_total_ms
metrics.computation: Wall-clock duration of the whole provider call, including every retry attempt. It is not the time of the successful attempt alone.

metrics.name: latency_ttft_ms
metrics.computation: Time from the request being sent to the first streamed token arriving. Emitted only for a streaming call; a non-streaming call has no first token to time.

metrics.name: throughput_tokens_per_sec
metrics.computation: Completion tokens divided by the generation duration. It measures output throughput, not the total call.

metrics.name: cost_usd
metrics.computation: Token counts priced by the provider's published rate for the model actually used. A model with no pricing entry emits no cost rather than a zero — a zero cost is a claim, and an absent one is a gap.

metrics.name: tokens_prompt
metrics.computation: Input tokens the provider reported for this call.

metrics.name: tokens_completion
metrics.computation: Output tokens the provider reported for this call.

metrics.name: tokens_thinking
metrics.computation: Reasoning tokens the provider reported, where the provider reports them separately from completion.

metrics.name: tokens_cache_read
metrics.computation: Prompt tokens served from the provider's cache.

metrics.name: tokens_cache_write
metrics.computation: Prompt tokens written into the provider's cache.

metrics.name: context_window_utilization
metrics.computation: Total tokens divided by the model's context window. Emitted only when the window is known; an unknown window emits nothing rather than assuming one.

metrics.name: reliability_error
metrics.computation: 1 when the call ended in an error, 0 otherwise. It counts terminal outcomes, not attempts.

metrics.name: reliability_timeout
metrics.computation: 1 when the terminal error was a timeout, 0 otherwise. A subset of reliability_error, not a separate failure.

metrics.name: reliability_retry_count
metrics.computation: HTTP attempts beyond the first. A call that succeeded first time is 0, not 1.

metrics.name: reliability_rate_limit_hit
metrics.computation: 1 when the provider returned a rate-limit response at any point during the call, 0 otherwise.

metrics.name: concurrency_calls_in_flight
metrics.computation: Concurrent provider calls observed during the run window. Run-scoped, so it carries the reserved node_id sentinel rather than a node's.

metrics.name: throughput_calls_per_sec
metrics.computation: Provider calls per second over the run window.

channels.label: curl | sh
channels.verification: the script verifies the sha256 against the release manifest and the manifest's ed25519 signature against a key pinned in the script, before placing anything on PATH; any failure is a hard stop

channels.label: PowerShell (irm | iex)
channels.verification: the script verifies the sha256 and then the ed25519 signature against a pinned key, before adding anything to PATH; any failure is a hard stop

channels.label: .deb package
channels.verification: the package's own sha256 is NOT in the signed release manifest (the manifest is signed before packaging runs). What the manifest covers is the binary INSIDE it, byte for byte: verify the heros-VERSION-linux-ARCH asset against SHA256SUMS, then confirm the installed /usr/bin/heros matches it
channels.pin: download {{deb}} for the exact version from that release and dpkg -i it

channels.label: .rpm package
channels.verification: the package's own sha256 is NOT in the signed release manifest (the manifest is signed before packaging runs). What the manifest covers is the binary INSIDE it, byte for byte: verify the heros-VERSION-linux-ARCH asset against SHA256SUMS, then confirm the installed /usr/bin/heros matches it
channels.pin: rpm -i the exact version's package URL, which ends in {{rpm}}

channels.label: container image
channels.verification: the image is digest-pinnable and is built in the same run from the same verified binary; pull by digest to pin exactly what you audited
channels.pin: docker run --rm ghcr.io/damonleelcx/heros:{{version}}   (or @sha256:… for a digest pin)

channels.label: Homebrew
channels.blocker: the formula is generated from the signed manifest and attached to every Release, but the tap repository heros-foreal/homebrew-tap does not exist yet and pushing to it needs a token secret. Until then `brew install heros-foreal/tap/heros` would fail
channels.verification: brew checks the sha256 in the formula, and the formula's sha256 is copied from the signed release manifest by the generator — so the chain to the signature is intact, with brew as the last link

channels.label: Scoop
channels.blocker: the manifest is generated and attached to every Release, but the bucket repository heros-foreal/scoop-bucket does not exist yet and pushing to it needs a token secret
channels.verification: scoop checks the hash in the manifest, and the generator copies that hash from the signed release manifest
channels.install: scoop bucket add heros https://github.com/heros-foreal/scoop-bucket; scoop install heros

channels.label: winget
channels.blocker: the three-file winget manifest is generated and attached to every Release, but publication is a pull request into microsoft/winget-pkgs whose review and merge are not ours to schedule
channels.verification: winget checks the InstallerSha256 in the manifest, which the generator copies from the signed release manifest
